chunks: Abu Khadijah Salim ibn Mukram al-Jammal narrated from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام that Dharih asked him:
about a slave who picks up lost property, so he said:

What has a slave to do with lost property? A slave does not own anything of himself, so the slave should not expose himself to it. Rather, it is fitting for a free person to announce it for a year in a public gathering. If its claimant comes, he should hand it over to him; otherwise, it becomes from his property. If he dies, it becomes an inheritance for his children and those who inherit from him. Then if its claimant comes after that, they should hand it over to him.

key_terms.الْحُرِّ: a free person with legal capacity to take responsibility for the item
key_terms.الْمَمْلُوكِ: a slave; one who does not possess independent ownership
key_terms.سَنَةً: a period of one full year for public announcement
key_terms.طَالِبُهَا: the claimant or owner seeking the lost property
key_terms.مِيرَاثًا: inheritance passed on to heirs after death
key_terms.يُعَرِّفَهَا: to publicly announce and identify the found property

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a slave or a free person handling lost property in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a fiqh ruling on lost property, stating that a slave should not take charge of luqaṭah because he does not independently own property. It also explains that a free person should publicly announce the item for one year, after which it may enter his property, though it must still be returned if the true owner later appears.
